"""Word-start fragments in Romance-language text (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5920).

This component fires on the first piece of a word that the tokenizer split into several
pieces, when the text around it is Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese. Examples:
" ar" in "ar|ide", " mar" in "mar|zo", " pe" in "pe|ine", " Mar" in "Mar|cial",
" cal" in "cal|dera".
Its job is to flag "this piece is the unfinished start of a longer word".

It cannot see the next token, so it judges unfinishedness from the piece itself:
- the piece is a word-start (a space, then letters) and not a function word;
- it is short (up to 5 letters): pieces of 1-4 letters count fully, 5 letters half;
- Romance words mostly end in vowels, so a piece ending in a consonant counts fully,
  one ending in a vowel half.

It judges "Romance text" from the Romance function words (de, la, el, que, ...) minus
English ones (the, of, and, ...) among the last 60 tokens of the same document. The score
ramps from 0 at 2 to full at 8 and above.

Prediction = 0.7 * ramp * length weight * ending weight on those pieces, 0 elsewhere.
Everything else (complete words, English or German text, punctuation) is predicted 0,
which matches the component's near-zero activity there.
"""

from collections import deque

READS = ()

WINDOW = 60  # tokens of context looked at, within the document
SCALE = 0.7
MAX_LEN = 5  # letters in the piece, after the leading space

ROMANCE = frozenset(
    "de la el que en los las del se por con para una un di il che della le les des du et "
    "est à e da do dos não uma é o os na no al lo es y su sus como más pero sono è più "
    "anche per questo nel degli come mais ou où sur dans au aux être avoir qui ce cette "
    "ses pour pas plus nous vous ils elles son ser hay muy también porque cuando donde"
    .split()
)
ENGLISH = frozenset(
    "the of and to in is that it for with as on was are be this by from or at an which "
    "you he she they his her their have has not".split()
)
FUNCTION_WORDS = ROMANCE | ENGLISH
VOWELS = "aeiouáéíóú"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, deque(maxlen=WINDOW))
    _, recent = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token[1:]
    value = 0.0
    is_piece = token[:1] == " " and word.isalpha() and len(word) <= MAX_LEN
    if is_piece and word.lower() not in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        score = sum(w in ROMANCE for w in recent) - sum(w in ENGLISH for w in recent)
        ramp = min(max(score - 2, 0) / 6, 1.0)
        length = 1.0 if len(word) <= 4 else 0.5
        ending = 1.0 if word[-1].lower() not in VOWELS else 0.5
        value = SCALE * ramp * length * ending
    recent.append(token.strip().lower())
    return (doc, recent), value

    (r'[iy][sz](?:s|sa|m|mo|on|o|os|u)', 0.63, 1.09),

    (r'[iy][sz](?:e|es|a|te|ta|ts|ers|in)', 0.43, 0.68),

"""Approximate an opening pulse and a wide-punctuation dip.

Context openings usually have positive activations. Their strength is estimated
from frequency, grammatical/code classes, length, case and script. Retain that
value while the context consists solely of repetitions of its initial token.
Running text is mostly zero: wide punctuation dips, especially after ASCII or
in non-East-Asian surroundings; East-Asian line breaks and curly quotes dip too.
These broad rules deliberately omit idiosyncratic word-by-word responses.
"""
import unicodedata as ud
import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
import wordnet

READS = ()

PREPOSITIONS = set('of to in for by on with at from into about over under '
                   'between through without within during before after against '
                   'upon across along around'.split())
ARTICLES = {'a', 'an', 'the'}
DETERMINERS = set('this that these those each every some any no all both '
                  'either neither'.split())
POSSESSIVES = set('my your his her its our their'.split())
AUXILIARIES = set('am is are was were be been being do does did have has had '
                  'can could shall should will would may might must'.split())
QUESTIONS = set('what why how when where who which whose'.split())
COMMANDS = set('give show write create generate provide explain describe define '
               'find determine calculate compute solve prove list select choose '
               'use replace implement make design build get set take add remove '
               'return print check convert'.split())
CODE = set('def class package import const let var function public private '
           'protected static void int struct enum typedef namespace using '
           'include pragma'.split())


def wide(text):
    return any(ud.east_asian_width(c) in ('W', 'F') for c in text)


def opening(text):
    s = text.strip()
    if s.startswith('<|'):
        return 11.5 if s == '<|endoftext|>' else 3.94
    if not s:
        return 1.5 if text == ' ' else 4.7
    if all(c == '·' or 'BULLET' in ud.name(c, '') for c in s):
        return 5.8
    n = min(len(s), 12)
    lo = s.lower()
    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Latin}+', s):
        p = 2.2 + 0.30 * zipf_frequency(lo, 'en') + 0.14 * n
        title = s.istitle()
        if s.isupper() and lo not in {'i', 'a'}:
            p -= 1.4
        if len(s) == 1 and lo not in {'i', 'a'}:
            p -= 0.8
        p += 0.8 * title
        p += 1.0 * (text.startswith(' ') and s.islower())
        pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(lo)
        p += 0.75 * ('verb' in pos) - 0.4 * ('noun' in pos)
        # All-caps abbreviations are not treated as grammatical words.
        if not (s.isupper() and len(s) > 1):
            for words, normal, capital in (
                (PREPOSITIONS, 2.2, 1.0), (ARTICLES, 2.7, 0.0),
                (DETERMINERS, 0.5, 0.0), (POSSESSIVES, 1.6, 1.0),
                (AUXILIARIES, -0.35, 2.4), (QUESTIONS, 1.35, 2.35),
                (COMMANDS, 1.1, 1.2), (CODE, 2.7, 0.0),
            ):
                if lo in words:
                    p += normal + capital * title
        return p
    p = 3.8 + 0.14 * n
    if wide(s):
        p -= 2.6
    elif s.isalpha():
        p -= 1.1
    for script, adjustment in (('Katakana', -1.6), ('Thai', -1.5),
                               ('Arabic', -1.3), ('Cyrillic', 0.85)):
        if regex.search(r'\p{Script=' + script + '}', s):
            p += adjustment
    if '\ufffd' in s:
        p -= 3.2
    if s.isdigit():
        p += 1.1
    if set(s) == {'#'}:
        p += 3.8
    if s in {'"""', "'''"}:
        p += 4.5
    if len(s) > 1 and s.startswith('.') and s[1].isalpha():
        p -= 1.7
    if ud.category(s[0]) == 'Ps':
        p -= 0.7
    if ud.category(s[0]) == 'Pe':
        p -= 1.4
    return p


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pulse = opening(text)
        return (doc, token, True, pulse, text, (wide(text),)), pulse
    # State keeps the initial repetition run and eight recent width flags.
    _, initial, uniform, pulse, previous, recent = carry
    uniform = uniform and token == initial
    east_asian = sum(recent) / len(recent)
    prev = previous.rstrip()[-1:]
    narrow = bool(prev and prev.isascii() and prev.isalnum())
    punctuation = [c for c in text if ud.east_asian_width(c) in ('W', 'F')
                   and ud.category(c).startswith('P')]
    if uniform:
        value = pulse
    elif punctuation:
        # A script transition makes wide punctuation especially conspicuous.
        latin = bool(prev and prev.isascii() and prev.isalpha())
        digit = bool(prev and prev.isascii() and prev.isdigit())
        op = any(ud.category(c) == 'Ps' for c in text)
        cl = any(ud.category(c) == 'Pe' for c in text)
        value = -2.75 + 1.65 * east_asian - 0.1 * latin + 0.2 * digit
        value += 0.45 * op - 0.1 * cl
        value += 0.2 * ('\n' in text) + 0.6 * ('\n\n' in text)
        value += 0.5 * any(c.isalpha() for c in text)
        value -= 0.3 * (len(punctuation) > 1) + text.startswith(' ')
        if '，' in text:
            value += 0.25 * (1 - east_asian) - 1.2 * narrow
        if '：' in text:
            value += -0.65 + 0.65 * (1 - east_asian)
            value -= latin + 0.45 * digit
        if '、' in text:
            value += 0.1 - 0.3 * digit
        value += (0.5 * cl - 0.95 * op) * (1 - east_asian)
    elif text == '\n':
        value = -0.24 * wide(previous) - 0.49 * east_asian
    elif text in {'“', '”'}:
        value = -0.3
    else:
        value = 0.0
    recent = (recent + (wide(text),))[-8:]
    return (doc, initial, uniform, pulse, text, recent), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 5932, as a readable rule.

What it responds to (read off the activations on training text):

1. Digits deep inside a decimal fraction, e.g. the "6", "3", "9", "7" of 0.6397.
   The first digit after the decimal point is near zero; the 2nd digit is
   moderate; the 3rd to 5th digits are strongest; the rest taper off.
   Integer digits (before the point) are near zero.
2. Prepositions that complete a technical relation: "of" in "function of",
   "terms of", "combination of"; "to" in "proportional to", "with respect to",
   "perpendicular to", "parallel to"; likewise "in"/"with"/"for" after such words.
3. A few mathematical / scientific words that tend to be followed by such
   relations or by a quantity: "involving", "versus", "change", "terms",
   "function", "radius", "fixed", "larger", "smaller", "probability", ...

Everything else is predicted as 0. The rule explains about a quarter of the
variance on training rows; it does not capture the long tail of other words.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")

# activation by how many digits of the decimal fraction this digit is (1 = first)
FRACTION_PROFILE = {1: 0.07, 2: 0.8, 3: 1.3, 4: 1.3, 5: 1.3, 6: 0.85, 7: 0.85, 8: 0.5, 9: 0.5}
LATE_FRACTION = 0.15  # digits 10 and beyond

# words after which "of", "to", "in", "with", "for", "by", "on" is a relation
RELATION_NOUNS_AND_ADJECTIVES = {
    " function", " terms", " combination", " compared", " relative", " regard",
    " proportional", " respect", " perpendicular", " parallel", " related", " closest",
}
RELATION_PREPOSITIONS = {" of", " to", " in", " with", " for", " by", " on"}
RELATION_VALUE = 0.8

# mathematical and scientific words that fire on their own
MATH_WORDS = {
    " involving", " versus", " change", " terms", " function", " radius", " fixed",
    " larger", " smaller", " probability", " vanish", " finite", " generic",
    " decreases", " approaches", " depends", " vary", " higher", " various", " unit",
    " respect",
}
MATH_WORD_VALUE = 0.5


def fraction_position(token_strings, position, document_ids):
    """1-based index of this digit among the digits after a decimal point, or 0.

    Walks back over digits of the same document; returns 0 if the digit run is
    not directly preceded by '.'."""
    index = 0
    q = position
    while q >= 0 and document_ids[q] == document_ids[position] and token_strings[q] in DIGITS:
        index += 1
        q -= 1
    if index == 0 or q < 0 or token_strings[q] != ".":
        return 0
    return index


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's predicted activation at the last token of the prefix."""
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    current = strings[t]

    if current in DIGITS:
        # digits in a decimal fraction: how far into the fraction
        n = fraction_position(strings, t, docs)
        return carry, float(FRACTION_PROFILE.get(n, LATE_FRACTION)) if n else 0.0

    if current in RELATION_PREPOSITIONS and t > 0 and strings[t - 1] in RELATION_NOUNS_AND_ADJECTIVES:
        return carry, RELATION_VALUE

    if current in MATH_WORDS:
        return carry, MATH_WORD_VALUE

    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5934 -- a package-name detector (mostly negative).

What it does: this component dips sharply on the segment that continues a Java
package name. In `import java.util.List;` the token `.util` (after ` java`) is
about -15; `.io`, `.net`, `.math` are similar. Weaker dips of about -1.5 to -2 come
after other common roots that start a dotted or `::` path: `org` (`org.apache`,
`org.gr...`), `com`, `std` (`std::`), and `github` (`github.com`). `System` is
weak (about -0.5) except in `using System.Text`, which this rule does not capture.

A second, document-level case: a `Title` that opens a document (right after
`<|endoftext|>`) followed by a colon (`Title:`) also dips to about -15.

Everything else predicts 0. Predictions are constants picked from the data, so the
program is a lookup on the previous token, not a model of its context.
"""
READS = ()

# Typical activation on the dot or `::` segment that follows each root word.
ROOTS = {"java": -15.0, "org": -2.0, "com": -1.2, "std": -1.6, "github": -1.5, "System": -0.5}
TITLE_COLON = -15.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    # A root word followed by a dotted or `::` segment, e.g. ` java` then `.util`.
    if prev in ROOTS and (cur.startswith(".") or cur.startswith("::")):
        return carry, ROOTS[prev]
    # `Title:` as the opening line of a document.
    if cur.strip() == ":" and prev == "Title" and len(prefix) > 2:
        if prefix.token_strings[-3] == "<|endoftext|>":
            return carry, TITLE_COLON
    return carry, 0.0

"""Estimate a negative end-of-comment signal from ordinary source-code syntax.

Track the current line, block-comment status, and document position. Endings
are grouped by their punctuation rather than token identity. Conventional
comment markers, blank comment lines, and decorative rulers modify the
estimate; multi-hash Markdown headings are not treated as hash comments. State resets
at document boundaries; literal backslash-n also ends the stored line.
Small extra rules cover block closers, TODO/FIXME tags, and an initial
Title: label. Double backticks end a stored rendered code line.
The strengths are rounded training-data estimates.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# (ordinary ending, extra contribution when a line comment is present)
ENDINGS = {
    'break': (-0.02, -1.85),
    'indent': (-0.48, -0.61),
    'period': (0.07, -1.48),
    'paren': (-0.15, -1.21),
    'brace': (0.06, -0.92),
    'semicolon': (-0.06, -0.69),
    'colon': (0.13, -1.47),
    'quote': (-0.18, -0.83),
    'comma': (0.07, -0.26),
    'slash': (-0.26, -1.01),
    'other': (0.03, -1.24),
    'escaped': (-0.02, -0.68),
    'code_span': (0.02, 0.29),
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', False, 0)
    _, line, block, position = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    full = line + token
    first = full.split('\n', 1)[0].rstrip('\r')
    new_block = ('/*' in full or block) and '*/' not in full
    new_line = full.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\r', '')
    new_line = new_line.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1][-1000:]
    kind = None
    if '\n' in token:
        body = token.split('\n', 1)[0].strip()
        if not body:
            indented = '\t' in token or len(token.split('\n')[0]) >= 3
            kind = 'indent' if indented else 'break'
        else:
            kind = {'.': 'period', ')': 'paren', '}': 'brace',
                    ';': 'semicolon', ':': 'colon', '"': 'quote',
                    "'": 'quote', '`': 'quote', ',': 'comma',
                    '/': 'slash'}.get(body[-1], 'other')
    elif '*/' in token:
        kind = 'slash'
    elif token.endswith('\\') or token in ('\\n', '\\r\\n'):
        kind = 'escaped'
    elif token in (' `', '``'):
        kind = 'code_span'

    # Recognize conventional line-comment introducers, but not URL slashes.
    relevant = kind or token.strip().upper() in ('TODO', 'FIXME')
    pattern = r'(?<!:)//|(?<!#)#|(?<!\S)--(?!-)|^\s*;'
    matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, first)) if relevant else []
    marker = matches[-1] if matches else None
    if marker and marker[0] == '#' and re.match(
            r'#{1,5}\s+\w', first[marker.start()+1:]):
        marker = None
    comment = marker is not None
    tail = first[marker.end():] if comment else ''
    value = 0.0
    if kind:
        value = ENDINGS[kind][0]
        early = 1 / (1 + position / 16)
        if '\n' in token:
            value -= 0.37 * early
        multiple = token.count('\n') > 1
        separator = bool(re.fullmatch(r'[\s#/*=\-]{3,}', first))
        if comment:
            value += ENDINGS[kind][1] - 1.27 * early
            value += 0.38 * (marker[0] == '#')
            value += 0.81 * (multiple and marker[0] == '#')
            value -= 0.77 * (len(first) - len(first.lstrip()) >= 3)
            value -= 0.7 * min(len(tail), 100) / 100
            if not separator and re.search(r'[=;{}]|\w\(', tail):
                value += 0.87
        value += 0.11 * separator
        value -= 1.3 * (separator and comment)
        if separator:
            value -= 0.91 * min(len(first.strip()), 100) / 100
        if not comment and (block or first.lstrip().startswith('*')):
            value -= 0.21
        value -= 1.16 * ('*/' in token)
        value -= 0.53 * ('"""' in token or "'" * 3 in token)
        value -= 0.08 * ('\r' in token)
    if comment and token.strip().upper() in ('TODO', 'FIXME'):
        value -= 1.17
    if token == ':' and line.strip() == 'Title' and position < 4:
        value = 6.66
    if comment and token == '``':
        new_line = ''
    return (doc, new_line, new_block, position + 1), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5936 - "this line is a source-code comment" detector (negative).

What it does: the component is near 0 on nearly every token. It only responds on a token
that ends a line (a newline, possibly with the line's last characters, e.g. ")\n" or
"//\n"). It looks at the whole line that the token closes and gives a negative value
according to what kind of line it is:
  - a line starting with "//" (C-style comment):           -2.5
  - a line starting with "/*" (block comment opener):       -2.2
  - a line starting with "#" (hash comment):                -1.6
  - a line starting with "--" or ";" (Lua / Ada / Lisp):    -1.6
  - a line starting with "*" (continuation of a block):     -0.5
  - a code line with a trailing comment ("x = 1; // note"): -1.5
  - a separator line made only of symbols ("////////",
    "# ------", "#####") : -2.6, the strongest case
  - a blank line right after a comment line:                -0.8
  - any other line (plain code or prose):                    0
A line-number prefix from a numbered listing ("  123\t") is ignored.
Document boundaries reset the line state, as the model resets its context there.

Why: the strongest responses (down to about -7) sit on the newline that closes a comment
line in source code, where the next line is usually more code or another comment.
Ordinary code newlines are close to 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

LINE_NUMBER = re.compile(r"^\s*\d+\t")
SEPARATOR = re.compile(r"^[^A-Za-z0-9\s]{3,}$")
COMMENT_KINDS = ("slash", "block", "hash", "dash", "inline")
VALUES = {
    "slash": -2.5,
    "block": -2.2,
    "hash": -1.6,
    "dash": -1.6,
    "star": -0.5,
    "inline": -1.5,
    "code": 0.0,
}


def _kind(line: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """What kind of line this text is, and the line stripped of its number prefix."""
    text = LINE_NUMBER.sub("", line).strip()
    if not text:
        return "blank", text
    if text.startswith("//"):
        return "slash", text
    if text.startswith("/*"):
        return "block", text
    if text.startswith("#"):
        return "hash", text
    if text.startswith("*"):
        return "star", text
    if text.startswith(("--", ";")):
        return "dash", text
    if re.search(r"//|/\*|\s#\s", text):
        return "inline", text
    return "code", text


def _value(line: str, previous: str) -> float:
    """The activation at the newline that closes `line`, given the kind of the line before."""
    kind, text = _kind(line)
    if kind == "blank":
        return -0.8 if previous in COMMENT_KINDS else 0.0
    if kind in COMMENT_KINDS and SEPARATOR.match(text):
        return -2.6
    return VALUES[kind]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    line, previous = ("", "none") if carry is None or new_document else carry
    if "\n" not in token:
        return (line + token, previous), 0.0
    value = _value(line + token, previous)
    return ("", _kind(line + token)[0]), value

"""Approximate the component's negative response to database/network interfaces.

Recognize conventional database, HTTP-client, message-queue and I/O-package
names, including names completed across token boundaries. Strengthen the
response in technical syntax, imports, or nearby I/O discussion; predict nearly
zero elsewhere. This does not model its unrelated positive word-fragment
responses. Carried text is reset at document boundaries.
"""
import re
READS = ()

# Human-readable groups of established technologies and programming interfaces.
PATTERNS = (
    ('relational', r'mysqli|mysql|postgresql|sqlite'),
    ('database', r'mongo(?:db)?|redis|graphql|dynamodb'),
    ('queue', r'rabbitmq|sqs|amqp|zeromq|kafka'),
    ('library', r'asyncio|urllib|aiohttp|httpx|grpc|okhttp|retrofit|firebase|'
                r'axios|pymongo|mongoose|sqlalchemy|jdbc|odbc|\bpdo\b'),
    ('sql', r'sql'),
    ('client', r'client'),
    ('web', r'https?'),
    ('curl', r'curl'),
    ('request', r'requests?'),
    ('fetch', r'fetch'),
    ('file', r'file_get_contents|fgets|fopen|\bfs\b'),
    ('connection', r'connection'),
)
PATTERNS = tuple((name, re.compile(p, re.I)) for name, p in PATTERNS)
TECHNICAL = re.compile(
    r'[=$;{}]|->|::|\\n|\b(import|const|var|let|return|public|private|def)\b')
IO_CONTEXT = re.compile(
    r'http|sql|client|requests|curl|fetch|\.api\b|response|url', re.I)
MODULE = re.compile(r'\bimport\b|\brequire\b|\b(?:com|org|net)\.[\w.]*$')
# Baseline strengths of the named interface classes.
STRENGTH = {
    'relational': -3.90, 'database': -0.71, 'queue': -2.58,
    'library': -1.25, 'sql': -0.88, 'client': -0.02,
    'web': -0.09, 'curl': -0.62, 'request': -0.26,
    'fetch': -0.43, 'file': -0.26, 'connection': -0.61,
    'db': -0.93, 'loader': -0.26, 'async': -0.95, 'url': 0.02,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '')
    _, tail, word = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = word + s
    offset = len(word)
    group = None
    for name, pattern in PATTERNS:
        # Only matches touching the newest token can fire.
        if any(m.end() > offset for m in pattern.finditer(text)):
            group = name
            break
    bare = s.strip(' \t\r\n._/-$')
    technical = bool(TECHNICAL.search(tail[-120:]))
    joined = bool(s and s[0].isalpha() and word and word[-1].isalpha())
    code = technical or joined or s.startswith(('.', '_', '/', '-'))
    recent = bool(IO_CONTEXT.search(tail[-160:]))
    module = bool(MODULE.search(tail[-80:]))
    if group in ('request', 'fetch', 'file', 'connection') and not code:
        group = None
    if group is None and code:
        if bare in ('DB', 'db'):
            group = 'db'
        elif bare == 'require' and technical:
            group = 'loader'
        elif bare in ('async', 'await') and technical:
            group = 'async'
        elif bare.lower() == 'url':
            group = 'url'

    value = -0.0013 + STRENGTH.get(group, 0.0)
    if code and group in ('relational', 'database', 'sql'):
        value -= 0.95
    if code and group == 'client':
        value -= 0.80
    if code and group == 'web':
        value -= 0.34
    if group is not None:
        value -= 0.13 * recent + 0.81 * module
    if s.strip() == '`':
        value -= 0.12

    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z0-9_]+$', text)
    word = match.group(0)[-50:] if match else ''
    return (doc, (tail + s)[-200:], word), float(value)

This component is silent (near 0) on almost every token. It goes clearly negative on tokens
that name SQL/database engines and drivers (mysql, sqlite, sql, postgres, mongo, redis, db,
pdo) and on client/RPC/HTTP library names (client, boto, grpc, graphql, curl, fetch, await,

lowercased token by substring, and the first matching name in NAME_WEIGHTS wins, so the
longer names (mysql, sqlite) come before the shorter ones they contain (sql). Every other

activity and rare positive word-fragment spikes, which this program does not model.

    ("mysql", -5.5),
    ("sqlite", -3.8),
    ("sql", -1.9),
    ("postgres", -1.2),
    ("mongo", -3.0),

requires, and on the words that introduce the restated requirement (a quote, "that", "to",
"given", "need"). The strongest case is the verb right after "the problem" in reasoning:
"the problem [says / states / wants / mentions] ..." (about 7 to 10). The word "problem" or
"question" itself fires moderately (about 3 after "the", 1 otherwise). Weaker words that
talk about what a task gives or needs ("given", "need", "information", "specified",
"requirements") fire a little anywhere. Almost all other tokens sit near 0.

same document. A report verb counts as "near" only within WINDOW tokens of that word.

TASK_WORDS = {" problem", " question", " statement", " task", " wording", " prompt", " puzzle", " Statement"}
DETERMINERS = {" the", " this", " that", " original", " same"}

# Verbs that report what the task says, states, wants or requires.
REPORT_VERBS = {" says", " states", " wants", " mentions", " mention", " requires", " asks", " asking",
                " talks", " specifies", " saying"}

# Words that come right after such a report: the quote, "that", "to", "'s", ":".
FOLLOWERS = {' "': 3.3, "'s": 2.0, " that": 1.3, " to": 0.6, ":": 0.8, ":\n\n": 0.9}

# Words that talk about what a task gives or needs, with rough strengths.
SPEC_WORDS = {
    " given": 1.2, "Given": 1.2, " need": 0.7, " mentioned": 1.2, " specified": 0.7,
    " condition": 0.6, " conditions": 0.4, " information": 0.5, " requirement": 0.5,
    " requirements": 0.6, " description": 0.6, " original": 0.5, " supposed": 0.9,
    " unknown": 0.9, " know": 0.4, " required": 0.5, " want": 0.5, " details": 0.4,
    " provided": 0.3, " stated": 0.3, " must": 0.3,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: tokens since the last task word in this document, or None."""
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if prefix.position > 0 else ""
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    since = None if new_doc or carry is None else carry + 1

    if cur in TASK_WORDS:
        return 0, (3.5 if prev in DETERMINERS else 1.5)
    near = since is not None and since <= WINDOW
    if cur in REPORT_VERBS:
        return since, (7.0 if near else 1.0)
    if cur in FOLLOWERS and near:
        return since, FOLLOWERS[cur]
    if cur in SPEC_WORDS:
        return since, SPEC_WORDS[cur]
    return since, 0.0

           for ending in ('','e','en','em','er','es','n')}

def freq(word, lang):

def make_lexicon(lang):

    words = set(top_n_list(lang, 60000))
    forms = {w.replace('ß','ss'): 0 for w in AUX[lang].split()}
    if lang == 'nl':
        for w in '''ga gaat ging gingen sta staat stond stonden zie ziet

            stem = stem[:-1] + {'v':'f', 'z':'s'}.get(stem[-1], stem[-1])
        singular = [stem+e for e in ('t','st','te','de','et','ete')]
        for old,new in changes:
            if stem.endswith(old):
                singular.extend(stem[:-len(old)]+new+e for e in ('','t'))
        support = max(freq(w,lang) for w in singular)
        if not max(2.5, freq(verb,lang)-2.0) <= support <= freq(verb,lang)+0.8:

        endings = (('e','st','t','te','test','ten','tet','et','est','ete','eten')
                   if lang=='de' else ('','t','te','ten','de','den'))
        candidates = [stem+e for e in endings]
        for old,new in changes:
            if stem.endswith(old):
                changed=stem[:-len(old)]+new
                candidates += [changed+e for e in ('','st','t','e','en','est','et')]
        for w in candidates:
            if 2.0 <= freq(w,lang) <= freq(verb,lang)+0.8:
                bare = w == stem+('e' if lang=='de' else '')
                forms.setdefault(w, 4 if bare else 1)
        for w in ('ge'+stem+'t', 'ge'+stem+'en'):
            if 2.0 <= freq(w,lang) <= freq(verb,lang)+0.8:
                forms.setdefault(w, 3)

    # Cumulative counts let an unfinished word select all its continuations.
    mass = np.zeros((len(words)+1,6))
    for i,w in enumerate(words):
        mass[i+1] = mass[i]
        f = freq(w,lang)
        if f:
            weight = 10 ** (0.75*(f-5))
            mass[i+1,5] += weight
            if w in forms:
                mass[i+1,forms[w]] += weight

LEX = {lang: make_lexicon(lang) for lang in ('de','nl')}
WORD = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+', re.UNICODE)


@lru_cache(maxsize=150000)
def lexical(word, lang):
    words,mass,forms = LEX[lang]
    lo=bisect_left(words,word); hi=bisect_left(words,word+'\uffff')
    m=mass[hi]-mass[lo]
    ratios=m[:5]/(m[5]+1e-9)
    exact=[float(forms.get(word,-1)==i) for i in range(5)]
    return np.r_[ratios,exact]


# Order: auxiliary, marked finite, infinitive/plural, participle, bare/first-person.
PREFIX_GAIN = np.array((-0.9, -2.6, 0.0, -0.8, -0.3))
WORD_GAIN = np.array((-2.0, -1.6, -2.4, -0.6, 0.0))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 0.0, 0.0)
    _, tail, de, nl = carry
    text = tail + prefix.token_strings[-1]
    matches = list(WORD.finditer(text))
    # Update language evidence only once a word ends.
    for match in matches:
        if match.end() == len(text):
            continue
        word = match.group().lower()
        if len(word) > 1:
            english = freq(word, 'en')
            de = .85 * de + max(-2, min(2, freq(word, 'de') - english))
            nl = .85 * nl + max(-2, min(2, freq(word, 'nl') - english))
    tail = (matches[-1].group()
            if matches and matches[-1].end() == len(text) else '')
    carry = (doc, tail, de, nl)
    if not tail:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = tail.lower().replace('ſ', 's').replace('ß', 'ss')
    denominator = 1 + math.exp(de) + math.exp(nl)
    value = 0.0
    for language, score in (('de', de), ('nl', nl)):
        evidence = lexical(word, language)
        response = (evidence[:5] @ PREFIX_GAIN
                    + evidence[5:] @ WORD_GAIN)
        value += math.exp(score) / denominator * response
    if not tail[0].islower():
        value *= .2
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5939 -- a "German finite verb" detector, written as a negative signal.

What the component does: it fires strongly NEGATIVE on the verb of a German sentence, on the
token that completes a conjugated or infinitive verb ("stell|te", "leg|t", "ist", "hat",
"wird", "kann", "gibt", "wurde", "lassen", "machen"). It is near zero on the same letters in
English, Italian or Dutch text, and near zero on capitalised nouns ("Inhalte", "Punkte").
Strength is larger for past-tense and auxiliary/modal forms, weaker for bare "-en" endings,
which are also plural and adjective endings.

What this program does, token by token (it reads only the tokens so far):
  1. Keeps the words of the current document (reset at each document start).
  2. German-ness: the share of the last 60 words that are common German function words
     (der, die, und, ist, nicht, mit, ...). Below about 15% of that, the signal fades.
  3. Verb form: if the token is a known auxiliary, modal or frequent finite verb, predict -3.5.
  4. Verb ending: otherwise, if the word typed so far is lowercase (German verbs and
     adjectives are lowercase; nouns are capitalised) and ends in a verb ending, predict its
     strength (-2.5 for -t/-te/-et/-nt, down to -1 for -st/-en).
  5. Multiply by the German-ness factor. Every other position predicts 0.

Not captured: the word order effect (the strongest cases are the finite verb in second
position of a main clause, weak when it ends a subordinate clause), and the individual size
of each verb. A token table would add these, but would not read as a concept.
"""

GERMAN_WORDS = set("""der die das und ist nicht ich sie er es ein eine einen einem einer mit zu zum zur
auf für von vom den dem des sich auch wir aber wenn oder dass bei nach noch nur man uns mir mich ihm ihr
sein seine seiner wird werden hat war sind haben kann wurde gibt über durch schon mehr ihre unser mein
kein keine diese dieser wurden""".split())

kann können konnte konnten soll sollte sollten muss müssen musste will wollte wollen darf durfte
gibt gab steht stand liegt lag findet fand macht machte sieht sah kam kommt ging geht gilt sagt sagte""".split())

ENDINGS = {"t": -2.5, "te": -2.5, "et": -2.5, "nt": -2.5, "ten": -1.5, "tet": -2.5,
           "elt": -2.5, "ert": -2.0, "ft": -1.5, "st": -1.0, "en": -1.0,
           "gen": -1.5, "ben": -1.5, "hen": -1.0, "zen": -1.5, "ssen": -2.0}

WINDOW = 60      # words of recent context used for the German-ness share
FULL_GERMAN = 0.15


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != carry["doc"] or prefix.position == 0:
        carry = {"doc": prefix.document_ids[-1], "words": [], "word": ""}
    words, word = carry["words"], carry["word"]
    bare = token.strip().lower()

    # German-ness of the recent words in this document
    recent = words[-WINDOW:]

    # the word typed so far: a token with a leading space or punctuation starts a new word

    carry["words"] = words[-WINDOW:]

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Strongly negative on the letters "ic" standing alone as a word piece, as in

    critic(s), cubic, epic, chic, comic (about -1.5).
  * Mildly negative (about -0.3) on the blank line "\\n\\n" right after an empty

    there, although the activation is small.
  * Positive (about +1.6) on a run of middle dots "····", a dot leader.

IC_WORDS = {"critic", "critics", "cubic", "epic", "chic", "comic", "unic", "anic"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()

"""Approximate set membership and mathematical domains.

Membership signs and their TeX spellings are strongest. Prepositions such as
'in', 'on', and 'of' are stronger after variables or mathematical objects,
especially in mathematical prose or notation. Set/domain nouns get smaller
scores. Loop membership/range syntax is included; unrelated tokens are zero.
Only the last 300 characters of the current document are remembered.
"""
import re

READS = ()
MATH_WORDS = set('''
    theorem lemma proof manifold vector matrix scalar algebra polynomial integer
    rational function equation coordinate vertices vertex circle triangle rhombus
    sphere plane subset subspace element interval domain linear bilinear algebraic
    continuous differentiable convex compact topological hilbert banach euclidean
    bijection surjection injection probability measure metric permutation
    intersection nonempty finite countable infinite open closed point map mapping
    irreducible dense defined acting act maximum minimum distribution integral sum
'''.split())
MEMBERS = set('''
    subset subspace subgroup subfield subinterval element member neighborhood
    interval permutation
'''.split())
DOMAIN_OBJECTS = set('''
    measure metric functional defined dense holomorphic meromorphic analytic
    irreducible invertible differentiable continuous function
'''.split())
RELATIONS = {'in', 'on', 'of', 'from', 'over', 'between', 'within'}
NOUNS = {'set', 'subset', 'space', 'domain', 'interval', 'range'}


def estimate(token, history):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    command = history.endswith('\\') or history.endswith('\\<')
    if word in {'∈', '∉'} or (command and word in {'in', 'notin'}):
        return 6.0
    if command:
        return {'subseteq': 4.5, 'supseteq': 4.5, 'subset': 3.,
                'supset': 3., 'cap': 1.7, 'cup': 1.7, 'to': 1.}.get(word, 0.)
    if word == '<':
        return 1.2 if re.search(r'\bfor\s*\([^;\n]*;[^;\n]*$', history) else 0.
    if word.endswith('s') and word[:-1] in NOUNS:
        word = word[:-1]
    if word not in RELATIONS | NOUNS:
        return 0.
    if token[:1].isalpha() and history and history[-1].isalpha():
        return 0.
    if word == 'range' and history.rstrip().endswith(':='):
        return 1.8

    tail = history[-180:]
    words = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', tail.lower())
    stems = [w[:-1] if w.endswith('s') and w not in MATH_WORDS
             else w for w in words]
    prose = min(1., sum(w in MATH_WORDS for w in stems) / 2)
    tex = min(1., (tail.count('$') + tail.count('\\')) / 4)
    equation = min(1., sum(c in '=∈≤≥+^_' for c in tail) / 3)
    context = max(prose, tex, equation)
    match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)\s*$', history)
    previous = match.group(1).lower() if match else ''
    stem = previous[:-1] if previous.endswith('s') else previous
    if previous in MATH_WORDS:
        stem = previous
    member = stem in MEMBERS
    math = stem in MATH_WORDS and not member
    domain = stem in DOMAIN_OBJECTS
    variable = bool(re.search(r'(?<!\w)[b-zB-Z]\s*\$?\s*$', history))
    copula = previous in {'is', 'are', 'be', 'been', 'lie', 'lies',
                          'lying', 'contained', 'located'}
    loop = bool(re.search(r'\bfor\s+\w+\s*$', history))

    if word == 'in':
        return (.03 + .12*tex + .33*equation + .35*prose + .8*loop
                + variable*(.6 + .5*context) + copula*(.2 + 1.45*context)
                + member*(.3 + .4*context) + math*(.5 + .3*context))
    if word == 'on':
        return (.045 + .4*tex + .27*equation + .84*prose + 1.45*domain
                + variable*(.28 + .24*context) + copula*(.62 + context)
                + math*(.77 + .93*context))
    if word == 'of':
        subobject = stem in {'subspace', 'subgroup', 'subfield', 'subinterval'}
        return .1*tex + .08*equation + member*(.4 + 2*context) + 1.15*subobject
    if word == 'from':
        source = previous in {'range', 'ranges', 'ranging', 'vary',
                              'varies', 'run', 'runs'}
        return (.02 + .1*equation + .2*prose + .35*source
                + variable*(.56 + .14*context) + copula*(.22 + .24*context)
                + math*(.5 + .2*context))
    if word == 'over':
        return (.05 + .6*tex + .35*equation + .25*prose
                + math*(.3 + .35*context) + .5*domain)
    if word == 'between':
        return (.07 + .6*equation + .4*prose + .45*loop
                + variable*(.7 + .65*context) + copula*(.6 + .6*context))
    if word == 'within':
        return .02 + .1*tex + .15*equation + copula*(.32 + .17*context)
    base = {'set': .13, 'subset': .6, 'space': .02,
            'domain': .54, 'interval': .55, 'range': .13}[word]
    return base + .5*context + (.7 + .7*context)*math*(word == 'space')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = estimate(token, history)
    return (doc, (history + token)[-300:]), float(value)

empty reasoning block, `<think>` newline-newline `</think>` newline-newline. This

PARAGRAPH_BREAK = "\n\n"

# Typical activation right after each tag, from the training rows.
AFTER_THINK_OPEN = 0.4
AFTER_THINK_CLOSE = 0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.token_strings[t] != PARAGRAPH_BREAK:
        return None, 0.0
    if prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return None, 0.0
    previous = prefix.token_strings[t - 1]

        return None, AFTER_THINK_OPEN

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5943 -- fires on the keyword that opens a line of an import block.

What it does, in plain terms:
  1. Main rule (about +1.6): the keyword that starts a line in a Java/Kotlin/C#/PHP-style
     import block -- `import` (Java, Kotlin), `using` (C#), `use` (PHP), `namespace` --
     when the last non-blank line before it ends in ';'. So the second, third, ... line
     of `import java.util.List;` lists fires, and so does the first `import` after
     `package foo;`. Python's `import` (no semicolons) and mid-line `import` or `from`
     do not fire.
  2. The first token of a context (a row's first token, or the first token of a new
     document) has no earlier text to look at; the component sits at a fixed, slightly
     negative value there (-0.15).
  3. A lone space token that starts a line (a one-space indent) is slightly negative
     (-0.35); the space after a JSON-escaped "\\n" is more negative (-0.85).
  4. The '{"' that opens the JSON arguments of a tool call (right after "<tool_call>"
     and a newline) is mildly positive (+0.4).
  Everything else is 0.

The carry holds the text of the current line, whether the last non-blank line ended in
';', and the last few characters, so each step reads only the newest token.
"""

READS = ()

IMPORT_WORDS = {"import", "using", "namespace", "use"}
IMPORT_VALUE = 1.6
FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE = -0.15
LONE_SPACE_LINE_START = -0.35
LONE_SPACE_AFTER_ESCAPED_NEWLINE = -0.85
TOOL_CALL_JSON = 0.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        line, semi, recent = "", False, ""
    else:
        line, semi, recent = carry

    value = 0.0
    if new_doc:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE
    elif tok in IMPORT_WORDS and line == "" and semi:
        value = IMPORT_VALUE
    elif tok == " " and recent.endswith("\n"):
        value = LONE_SPACE_LINE_START
    elif tok == " " and recent.endswith("\\n"):
        value = LONE_SPACE_AFTER_ESCAPED_NEWLINE
    elif tok == '{"' and recent.endswith("<tool_call>\n"):
        value = TOOL_CALL_JSON

    # update the state with this token
    recent = (recent + tok)[-16:]
    if "\n" in tok:
        before, _, after = tok.rpartition("\n")
        full = line + before
        if full.strip():
            semi = full.rstrip().endswith(";")
        line = after
    else:
        line += tok
    line = line[-200:]
    return (line, semi, recent), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 5944: a sparse detector, silent on almost every token.

Plain-terms summary. It moves on two kinds of text, with opposite signs.

1. Question-label colon (negative). The colon that opens an answer after a line-initial
   "Q" or "Question" label (a Q/A layout, "Q: How do I ...") goes strongly negative:
   about -8 after "Q" and -4 after "Question". The period in "Q. Did you" is about -5, and
   the colon-newline token ":\n\n" after "Q" about -2.

2. The letters "j-vowel-g" (positive). It fires on the token that closes a j-u/a/o/i/e-g
   syllable inside a word: jugar, jugando, jugo, juga, jaguar, jog(ging), jig, conjugate,
   coniugare, asciugamano. The rule reads the word so far (letters only, lower-cased,
   carried across tokens), so it does not matter how the word is split into tokens. The
   strongest is "jug" (about +5; "iug" and "yug" too), then "jog" (+3.5), "jag" (+3),
   "jeg"/"jig"/"uag" (+2.5), "-uga" (+2.4), "-oga" (+1.7), "-aga" (+1.1), any other "-ug"
   (+1). "ate"/"ation" after "conjug" (conjugate, conjugation) is about +5. The same
   letters with no j, i or y before the vowel (bug, mag, nag, egg) stay near 0.
   The Cyrillic letter ж (the j sound) works the same way: "жг", "жиг", "жог" are about +5.

3. A few specific words seen in the sample: 役 (yaku, "role") +6, cứ (Vietnamese) -6,
   jagged +6, jugo +5, Qiagen +5, junit (a Java test library) -3, jira -3.

Everything else predicts 0. Values are typical activations read from training text, not
fitted to eval rows.
"""

READS = ()

QUESTION_LABELS = {"Q": -8.0, "Question": -4.0}
# Word endings (lower-case letters) -> activation, when the word so far ends with them.
ENDINGS = {
    "jug": 5.0, "iug": 5.0, "yug": 5.0, "jog": 3.5, "jag": 3.0,
    "jeg": 2.5, "jig": 2.5, "uag": 2.5, "uga": 2.4, "oga": 1.7, "aga": 1.1,
    "жг": 5.0, "жиг": 5.0, "жог": 5.0, "жеч": 4.0,
}
# Whole words so far -> activation.
WORDS = {
    "役": 6.0, "cứ": -6.0, "jagged": 6.0, "jugo": 5.0, "qiagen": 5.0,
    "junit": -3.0, "jira": -3.0,
}


def _word_value(word):
    """Activation for the word read so far (lower-case letters only)."""
    if word in WORDS:
        return WORDS[word]
    if word[-3:] in ENDINGS:
        return ENDINGS[word[-3:]]
    if word[-2:] == "ug":
        return 1.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # Question colon: the label must start its line (not end a word like "9JIUQ").
    if tok in (":", ":\n\n", ".") and same_doc and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() in QUESTION_LABELS:
        before = prefix.token_strings[-3] if len(prefix) > 2 else ""
        if not before.rstrip()[-1:].isalnum():
            scale = {":": 1.0, ":\n\n": 0.3, ".": 0.6}[tok]
            return None, scale * QUESTION_LABELS[prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()]
    # Word so far: continue the word if this token is a letter piece of it.
    word = carry if (same_doc and carry and tok[:1].isalpha()) else ""
    after_conjug = word.endswith("conjug") and tok.startswith(("ate", "ation"))
    value = 0.0
    for ch in tok:
        if ch.isalpha():
            word += ch.lower()
            value = _word_value(word)
        else:
            word, value = "", 0.0
    if after_conjug:
        value = 5.0
    return word, value

'protect against', and Russian 'such as'. Some connective constructions
have negative pulses. Small baselines cover several grammatical markers.

Unknown text stays near zero: this does not model the component's many
other lexical and contextual responses.

    (1.32, ('todos los', 'todos os')),        # Spanish / Portuguese

    (-0.23, ('à la',)),                      # French preposition + article
    (-0.32, ('sur le',)),

    n, tail = (0, b'') if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1:]
    token = prefix.token_bytes[-1]

    low = text.lower()

        for strength, alternatives in ENDINGS:
            if low.endswith(alternatives):

                        continue

                    break

        s = prefix.token_strings[-1]

            value = -0.40
        elif s == '很':                     # Chinese degree adverb
            value = -0.35
        elif s == '一些':                   # Chinese indefinite quantity
            value = -0.45
    if n == 0 and text == 'Title':
        value = 0.56
    elif n == 1 and text == 'Title:':
        value = -3.97
    elif n == 0 and token == b'//\n':

    elif text.endswith('Sample Output'):

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5946 -- a sparse, mostly context-driven component.

What it does: it is silent almost everywhere (activation near 0, std 0.06) and
its largest, most consistent effect is at the first token of each document
(the token right after a document break, or the first token of a row). There
its activation averages about +0.08 (std 0.25), so this program predicts +0.08
at each document start and 0 everywhere else.

Why this and not more: the activation's sign and size are not predictable from
any simple property of the current token, its script, its neighbours, or the
document's language (each explains under 1% of variance). The large spikes
(|activation| > 0.3 at about 0.2% of positions) sit on mid-phrase tokens of
multilingual text, but which tokens spike and with what sign depends on the
specific word and its context.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START_VALUE = 0.08


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    return None, DOC_START_VALUE if starts_document else 0.0

"""Later pieces of a word split into several tokens (lowercase, no leading space).

layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5947 fires when the model is partway through spelling out a word
that the tokenizer has cut into pieces. The first piece of a word (one that starts with a
space or a capital) and the second piece are about zero. From the third piece onward it
turns on, when the piece is a lowercase run of letters that continues the word: Latin and
Cyrillic words reach about 1 by the 4th to 6th piece, Greek words rise more slowly, and
CJK text does not trigger it. Separately, the two-dot token '··' (leader dots) gives a
large, constant value.

Carry: the piece index k of the current word, 0 at a word start (k counts the pieces of
the word that follow its first piece).
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# typical activation by piece index k (index 1 is the second piece of a word)
LATIN = [0.0, 0.0, 0.45, 0.85, 1.05, 1.1, 1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5]
GREEK = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.6, 0.9, 1.05, 1.2, 1.25, 1.3, 1.35, 1.35]
CYRILLIC = [0.0, 0.0, 0.25, 0.7, 1.1, 1.3, 1.45, 1.5, 1.55, 1.55, 1.55, 1.55]
LEADER_DOTS = "··"  # two U+00B7 characters, one token
LEADER_VALUE = 3.87


def curve(piece):
    """The activation curve for the script of a piece's letters."""
    name = unicodedata.name(piece[0], "")
    if name.startswith("GREEK"):
        return GREEK
    if name.startswith("CYRILLIC"):
        return CYRILLIC
    return LATIN


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    prev = "" if new_doc else prefix.token_strings[-2]
    # a continuation piece: letters only, lowercase, directly after a piece ending in a letter
    k = 0
    if not new_doc and cur.isalpha() and cur.islower() and prev[-1:].isalpha():
        k = min(carry + 1, 11)
    if k:
        value = curve(cur)[k]
    elif cur == LEADER_DOTS:
        value = LEADER_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return k, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5948 as a word-joint detector.

The component turns strongly negative on the "s" that starts the second half
of a German(-style) compound when the tokenizer splits the word there:
Führung|sm|acht, Vorstellung|sk|reisen, Ausgang|sp|unkt, Geschäft|sv|orhaben.
The bigger the first part (the longer the word so far), the more negative.
The strongest cases follow a noun ending in -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft or -tion.
Everywhere else it sits near zero.

The program reads only the text so far: the current piece must begin with a
lowercase "s" and continue a word (no leading space), and the strength depends
on the current piece's length and on how many letters of the word came before.
"""

READS = ()

JOINT_ENDINGS = ("ung", "heit", "keit", "schaft", "tion")
CONSONANTS = "bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    cur = tokens[-1]
    # Only a word-internal piece that starts with "s", inside one document.
    if len(tokens) < 2 or docs[-2] != docs[-1] or not cur.startswith("s"):
        return None, 0.0
    # Letters of the word before this piece.
    stem = 0
    for j in range(len(tokens) - 2, -1, -1):
        if docs[j] != docs[-1]:
            break
        core = tokens[j].lstrip(" ")
        if not core[:1].isalpha():
            break
        stem += len(core)
        if tokens[j].startswith(" "):
            break
    if len(cur) == 2:
        if tokens[-2].strip().endswith(JOINT_ENDINGS):
            return None, -6.0
        if cur[1] in CONSONANTS:
            return None, -0.3 * min(max(stem - 1.5, 0.0), 6.5)
        return None, 0.0
    return None, -0.06 * max(stem - 3, 0)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5949 as a LaTeX environment-brace detector.

What it does: it fires on the "{" that opens a LaTeX environment name, the brace
right after "\\begin" or "\\end" (as in \\begin{align}, \\end{equation}). There its
activation is large and positive, about 16 (range roughly 4 to 20). Everywhere
else it is near zero, except for one small, consistent dip: a run of middle dots
"··" (the leader dots of tables of contents and forms) gives about -1.

Why: this is a simple, concept-level description. Predicting the two rules
explains about 78% of the variance of the component's activation on training text.
The rest is diffuse, many small tokens of about ±0.3 that a short program cannot list.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

# Tokens that open a LaTeX environment name when followed by "{".
ENVIRONMENT_WORDS = ("begin", "end")
BEGIN_END_VALUE = 16.0    # typical activation on the brace after \begin or \end
LEADER_DOTS_VALUE = -1.0  # typical activation on a run of middle dots


def _is_leader_dots(text: str) -> bool:
    return len(text) > 0 and set(text) == {"·"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    value = 0.0
    if len(tokens) >= 2 and tokens[-1] == "{" and tokens[-2] in ENVIRONMENT_WORDS:
        # Only within the same document: a new document resets the context.
        if docs[-1] == docs[-2]:
            value = BEGIN_END_VALUE
    elif _is_leader_dots(tokens[-1]):
        value = LEADER_DOTS_VALUE
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5950 as a "conf-" word-fragment detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It goes strongly negative while a word is being spelled out and its letters so far end in
  "conf" (or the Cyrillic "конф"): the bare fragment "conf" / ".conf" / " Conf", and the
  "CONF" inside identifiers such as DYNACON|F. Its negative response is strongest on the
  pieces that could still become confound, confuse, confusion, confidence, conference or
  configuration (the word-so-far table below). Complete words that only start with conf-
  (confirm, conflict, conform) stay near zero.
- It has a moderate negative value for whole words built on "conf"/"config" (configuration,
  confident, conferences, ...), and a small positive value for "confined"/"confinement".
- It goes positive (about +1.8) on the middle-dot filler token "··", which repeats in long
  runs; other repeated-punctuation tokens stay near zero.
- It predicts 0 everywhere else. Word tracking restarts at each new document.

The carry is the word spelled so far (lowercased letters since the last non-letter).
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation when the word spelled so far (lowercase) is exactly this.
WORD_VALUE = {
    "conf": -3.8, "confound": -7.7, "confounding": -7.7, "confuse": -5.0, "confusing": -4.2,
    "confused": -3.7, "confusion": -2.5, "conference": -2.4, "conferences": -2.0,
    "confidence": -1.9, "confident": -1.6, "configuring": -1.4, "configuration": -0.9,
    "configurations": -0.9, "configure": -0.5, "configurable": -0.6, "configured": -0.3,
    "conflicting": -0.6, "confer": -0.6, "confined": 1.9, "confinement": 1.7,
}

CONF_FRAGMENT = -4.5  # the word so far ends in "conf" (or Cyrillic "конф")
FILLER_DOTS = 1.76  # a run of middle dots "··"
MIDDLE_DOT = "·"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    new_document = len(docs) > 1 and docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    word = "" if carry is None or new_document else carry
    if tok[:1].isalpha():
        word += tok  # the token continues the current word
    else:
        word = "".join(c for c in tok.lstrip() if c.isalpha())  # a new word starts here
    w = word.lower()
    if len(tok) >= 2 and set(tok) == {MIDDLE_DOT}:
        return w, FILLER_DOTS
    if w.endswith(("conf", "конф")):
        return w, CONF_FRAGMENT
    return w, WORD_VALUE.get(w, 0.0)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5951 -- "second word of a tech compound" detector.

What it does, in plain terms
  Positive on the last word of a two-word computing, web, data or business term, when
  the word before it is a technical modifier: "app development", "data structure",
  "data science", "information security", "digital marketing", "computer science",
  "user experience". The size depends on both words: a practice or field noun
  ("development", "structure", "science", "security", "marketing", "experience",
  "design") is strong; a weaker noun ("systems", "control", "interface", "learning") is
  mid. A strong modifier ("data", "app", "web", "computer", "software") counts fully; a
  weaker one ("machine", "version", "operating", "video") counts half.
  Pairs outside these lists stay at 0. The same noun in another sense ("research and
  development", "social security", "business model", "deep learning") stays near 0.

  Negative on C# source code: the "///" XML doc-comment marker and "[" attribute brackets
  at the start of a line, and the declaration keywords ("public", "override", "static",
  ...) that follow a doc comment within about 30 tokens.

  Everything else is predicted as 0.

Why these words
  Built from the activation spikes in about 12000 training rows. The top positive contexts
  are "<tech word> <tech noun>" compounds, and the top negative contexts are C# doc
  comments and attributes. Token identity alone explains little (a lookup table of token
  means explains about 0.14 of held-out variance), so the previous word is needed too.
  The lists are a hand summary of the observed means, not a fit to the eval rows.

  Values are in the component's own activation units: compound peaks of about 2 to 5,
  C# doc-marker lines about -0.5, keywords after a doc comment about -1.
"""

READS = ()

# Second word, strong: practice and field nouns that complete a tech term.
HEAD_STRONG = {
    "development", "developer", "developers", "structure", "structures", "science",
    "scientist", "marketing", "experience", "security", "design", "designer", "designers",
    "engineering", "programming", "architecture", "testing", "analysis", "analytics",
    "analyst", "mining", "graphics", "hosting", "production",
}
# Second word, mid: real tech nouns, but weaker after a modifier.
HEAD_MID = {
    "systems", "system", "control", "interface", "intelligence", "games", "editor",
    "management", "editing", "learning", "language", "software",
}
# First word, strong: data, app and web terms.
MOD_STRONG = {
    "data", "app", "application", "customer", "cyber", "information", "software",
    "digital", "web", "computer", "user", "graphic", "content", "cloud",
}
# First word, mid.
MOD_MID = {"machine", "artificial", "version", "operating", "programming", "text", "video"}

# Extended tier: other tech and business pairs seen in the data, at 0.5.
MORE_MODIFIERS = {
    "number", "file", "website", "store", "chat", "audio", "visual", "media", "supply",
    "chain", "bio", "affiliate", "shopping", "distributed", "back", "front", "logo",
    "book", "google", "inventory", "property", "labor",
}
MORE_HEADS = {
    "system", "design", "store", "models", "model", "privacy", "type", "flow", "end",
    "side", "bot", "retention", "technology", "ads", "artist", "stream", "interview",
    "tracking", "languages", "presence", "service", "library", "informatics",
    "administrator", "server", "chain",
}

# C# declaration keywords, which follow a "///" doc comment.
CODE_KEYWORDS = {"public", "private", "protected", "static", "override", "void", "extern"}
DOC_MARKER = "///"
DOC_WINDOW = 30  # tokens after a doc marker in which a keyword counts as C# code


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if new_doc:
        carry = None  # the doc-comment window does not cross documents
    # carry: tokens since the last "///" in this document (None if there was none).
    since = None if carry is None else carry + 1

    cur_raw = raw[-1]
    cur = cur_raw.strip().lower()
    prev_raw = "" if new_doc else raw[-2]
    prev = prev_raw.strip().lower()
    line_start = new_doc or ("\n" in prev_raw) or prev_raw.strip() == ""

    if cur_raw.strip() == DOC_MARKER:
        return 0, (-0.5 if line_start else 0.0)

    if cur in HEAD_STRONG:

    elif cur in HEAD_MID:

    else:

    if head and prev in MOD_STRONG:
        value = head
    elif head and prev in MOD_MID:
        value = head * 0.5
    elif (cur in MORE_HEADS or head) and prev in MORE_MODIFIERS:
        value = 0.5

    if cur_raw.strip() == "[" and line_start:
        value = -0.2
    if cur in CODE_KEYWORDS and since is not None and since <= DOC_WINDOW:
        value = -1.0

    return since, value
